text:
Self-metathesis of a terminal alkene, RCH=CH₂, with the Grubbs catalyst gives the olefin-exchange product  

 2  RCH=CH₂  ⟶  RCH=CHR  +  CH₂=CH₂  

Ethene (CH₂=CH₂) is to be ignored, so only the internal alkene RCH=CHR has to be considered.

For 3-methylpent-1-ene the group “R” is 3-methyl-butyl containing a stereogenic centre (marked *):  
 R = CH₃–CH₂–C*(CH₃)–CH₂–  (the *-carbon is chiral).

Because the starting material is racemic, both the R* and S* enantiomers of the alkyl group are present.  
When two such alkenes undergo self-metathesis the double bond product can have:

1. Nature of the two alkyl groups attached to the C=C
   a) R* / R*  (or S* / S*) – the two groups are enantiomeric; they give the same constitutional product but as a pair of enantiomers (RR and SS).
   b) R* / S* – the two sides differ in configuration (RS, identical with SR).

2. Geometry about the new C=C bond  
   Each of the above constitutional possibilities can be either E (trans) or Z (cis), because each vinylic carbon bears R* (or S*) and H.

Hence:

• RR (racemic RR/SS) – E  
• RR (racemic RR/SS) – Z  
• RS (meso) – E  
• RS (meso) – Z  

This gives a total of 4 distinct products (ethene excluded; enantiomeric pairs counted as one product).

Therefore the number of possible products is 4.

Answer: C
